title: Cohomology on a chosen compactification
statement:
Use the finite coefficient
ring $A$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ be a
compactification
of $a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$, with proper map $\bar a:\bar X\to s$.
For a bounded
constructible complex $K$ equipped with an
explicit etale-origin
witness, there is a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
C_{j,K}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!K).
$$

Here $j_!K$ is extension by
zero, and the ordinary
and compact-support cohomology use the
fiber over $s$.
The comparison respects changes of compactification.

proof.text: Work with the coefficient and geometric data of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $A=A_{E,n}$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, and $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ separated of finite type. Thus $X$ and $s$ are finite-type $k$-schemes and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. Let $c=(j,\bar a)$ be the given compactification in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Retain the specified witness $(L,\alpha)$, $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Since $K$ is bounded it is bounded below; with this witness it is an object of $\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(X,A)$ of [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], whose morphisms are all ambient morphisms between the underlying complexes. If $c_*$ is the compactification used to define $Ra_{X!}$, [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and [def-weil-compact-support-candidate] give $Ra_{X!}=Ra_{X!}^{c_*}$ and $Ra_{X!}^{c}=R\bar a_*j_!$, where $j_!$ is the termwise extension by zero specified by the candidate definition.

source.place: First paragraph, candidate formula and explicit etale-origin domain

proof.text: Apply [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] with base field $K_0=k$, $f=a_X$, and compactifications $c_*,c$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1, including the finite coefficient $A_{E,n}$ and the explicit etale-origin witness. It gives a natural comparison isomorphism $\theta_{c_*,c}:Ra_{X!}^{c_*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X!}^{c}$ on that domain, independent of the common refinement used. Hence its component is an isomorphism $\theta_{c_*,c,K}:Ra_{X!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar a_*j_!K$ in the derived category over $s$. This uses the natural comparison and independence asserted in the proposition's statement, not a property merely postulated in a definition.

source.place: First paragraph, comparison with the chosen candidate

proof.text: The bounded constructible hypothesis on $K$, with exactly the finite-torsion convention of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], permits [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] to be applied to $a_X:X\to s$, with $K_0=k$ and coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$. Its restriction $Ra_{X!}:D^b_c(X,A)\to D^b_c(s,A)$ gives $Ra_{X!}K\in D^b_c(s,A)$. By the isomorphism in Step 2 the object $R\bar a_*j_!K$ is also in $D^b_c(s,A)$: an isomorphism preserves each cohomology sheaf up to isomorphism, so it preserves both the finite nonzero range and constructibility. Thus the functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,A)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] applies to both sides. Set $C_{j,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_{c_*,c,K})$. Its inverse is $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_{c_*,c,K}^{-1})$, by the functor laws. By the formulas in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], its source is $R\Gamma_c(X,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}K)$ and its target is $R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(R\bar a_*j_!K)$. For the input of the ordinary-cohomology notation, also apply [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] to the separated finite-type open immersion $j:X\to\bar X$. Here $\bar a$ is separated and of finite type because it is proper, by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. In the triangle $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar a}s$, the finite-type morphism $a_X$ and separated target morphism $\bar a$ satisfy [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], so $j$ is quasi-compact. (Equivalently, its current quasi-compact/quasi-separated formulation applies: finite type implies quasi-compact, and a closed diagonal is quasi-compact.) Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes $j$ finite type. The open immersion identifies $X$ with an open subscheme of $\bar X$, hence $X\times_{\bar X}X=X$ and $\Delta_j$ is the identity, a closed immersion; $j$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its compactification $(j,\operatorname{id}_{\bar X})$ has candidate $R(\operatorname{id}_{\bar X})_*j_!=j_!$ by [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]: direct image by the identity is the identity exact functor, so its derived functor is the identity. Coherence on our witnessed object identifies this candidate with the compact-support functor for $j$. Thus the same restriction theorem gives $j_!K\in D^b_c(\bar X,A)$, as required to use the ordinary-cohomology definition. These are precisely the coefficient complexes in the assertion.

source.place: Second paragraph, apply the fibre functor; domain justified by compact-support bounded constructibility

proof.text: For any morphism $h:K\to K'$ between bounded constructible complexes with witnesses, it is a morphism of the witnessed domain by [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Naturality in [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] says $(R\bar a_*j_!)(h)\circ\theta_{c_*,c,K}=\theta_{c_*,c,K'}\circ Ra_{X!}(h)$. Apply $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and its preservation of composition. The resulting equality is $R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!h)\circ C_{j,K}=C_{j,K'}\circ R\Gamma_c(X,h)$, with notation given by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. This proves naturality for all such $h$, without imposing an extra compatibility hypothesis on $h$.

For two compactifications $c_i=(j_i,\bar a_i)$, let $\theta_{c_1,c_2}$ be the natural comparison of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]. Its cocycle identity gives $\theta_{c_1,c_2,K}\circ\theta_{c_*,c_1,K}=\theta_{c_*,c_2,K}$. All three values lie in $D^b_c(s,A)$ by Step 3. Apply the functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] to obtain $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_{c_1,c_2,K})\circ C_{j_1,K}=C_{j_2,K}$. The proposition asserts that $\theta_{c_1,c_2}$ is independent of the common refinement, is the prescribed comparison for a refinement, and is the identity for an identity refinement. The same assertions survive applying a functor, and the displayed equality gives precisely the asserted compatibility under changes of compactification, including their compositions.

source.place: Final paragraph, cocycle compatibility under changes of compactification

proof_origin.place: Entire proof; explicit naturality and cocycle equations, and fibre-functor domain check expanded from its two paragraphs
